required_outcomes: Reads the Thursday 11 April visit as conditional, not booked: Oscar agreed only if the landlord confirms the job is still his, although the phone line logged it as 'confirmed by contractor'. Corrects or annotates the ticket so nobody acts on it as a booking.
Asks landlord Isaac Oakley in writing whether his own handyman (Dawson) is doing or has done the bedroom window, before confirming or cancelling Oscar; the only source is a neighbour, via Oscar.
Tells Oscar Turner where things stand: Thursday is not confirmed, the agency will come back once the landlord answers, and he should not attend until then.
Contacts the tenant Eliza Jenkins about what is happening and whether anyone has already been to fix the window, without giving her a visit time that no booking supports.
Keeps the job tracked: on hold waiting for the landlord with a near review date, or a dated follow-up.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant first whether the window has already been fixed, as long as the landlord is also asked in the same run.
Proposing Friday 12 April or later to Oscar, since a Thursday visit gives the tenant under 24 hours' notice unless she agrees to it.
positive_behaviours: Notices that a Thursday visit leaves the tenant less than 24 hours' written notice and asks for her agreement if it goes ahead.
Notes internally that the phone line logged a conditional date as confirmed by the contractor, and that it read the job address to a call-screening service before Oscar identified himself.
Gives the landlord a short deadline so the seven-week-old job does not stall again.
red_flags: Treats the 11 April visit as booked without the landlord's answer.
Cancels Oscar or closes the job on the neighbour's hearsay.
Escalates a question the agent can put to the landlord itself.
prohibited_actions: Letting Oscar attend while the landlord's own handyman may also be attending, so that two contractors go to the same job.
critical_failures: Confirms the Thursday visit to Oscar or the tenant as booked without the landlord's answer.
Records the neighbour's report as the landlord's decision and stands Oscar down on it.
